events.title: Athens surrenders to Sparta, ending the Peloponnesian War
events.description: Athens, blockaded by the Spartan admiral Lysander and King Pausanias, surrendered, ending the Peloponnesian War between the Athenian-led Delian League and the Spartan-led Peloponnesian League. The defeat of Athens began a period of Spartan hegemony over Greece.

events.title: The Abbasids crush rebel Armenian princes at Bagrevand
events.description: At Bagrevand, the caliphal army crushed Armenian princes who had rebelled against the Abbasid Caliphate, killing their main leaders and almost extinguishing the power of the Mamikonian family. It signalled the start of large-scale Armenian migration into the Byzantine Empire.

events.title: Montagu's Yorkist army defeats the Duke of Somerset at Hedgeley Moor
events.description: In the Wars of the Roses, a Yorkist army under John Neville, Baron Montagu, defeated a Lancastrian army under Henry Beaufort, Duke of Somerset, at Hedgeley Moor. Montagu was the younger brother of Richard Neville, Earl of Warwick, the Kingmaker.

events.title: Saint-Dié scholars publish the book that names America
events.description: The Cosmographiae Introductio, issued with Martin Waldseemüller's world map, proposed naming the New World 'America' after Amerigo Vespucci. The only surviving copy of the map is in the Library of Congress.

events.title: Last Ming emperor takes his own life as Beijing falls
events.description: As Li Zicheng's rebels entered Beijing, the Chongzhen Emperor hanged himself on Coal Hill behind the Forbidden City. Within weeks the Manchus seized the capital and founded Qing rule.
events.html: As Li Zicheng's rebels entered Beijing, the Chongzhen Emperor hanged himself on Coal Hill behind the Forbidden City. Within weeks the Manchus seized the capital and founded Qing rule.

events.title: Work begins on the Suez Canal
events.description: Ferdinand de Lesseps struck the first blow at the site of Port Said. The canal opened in 1869, linking the Mediterranean and the Red Sea and shortening the sea route from Europe to Asia.
events.html: Ferdinand de Lesseps struck the first blow at the site of Port Said. The canal opened in 1869, linking the Mediterranean and the Red Sea and shortening the sea route from Europe to Asia.

events.title: Allied troops land at Gallipoli
events.description: British, French, Australian and New Zealand troops landed on the Gallipoli peninsula. The campaign failed after eight months and around 100,000 deaths on both sides; 25 April is now Anzac Day.
events.html: British, French, Australian and New Zealand troops landed on the Gallipoli peninsula. The campaign failed after eight months and around 100,000 deaths on both sides; 25 April is now Anzac Day.

events.title: Watson and Crick publish the double helix
events.description: Nature published James Watson and Francis Crick's paper on the structure of DNA, alongside papers by Maurice Wilkins and Rosalind Franklin's group. It explained how genetic information is copied.
events.html: Nature published James Watson and Francis Crick's paper on the structure of DNA, alongside papers by Maurice Wilkins and Rosalind Franklin's group. It explained how genetic information is copied.

events.title: Carnation Revolution topples Portugal's dictatorship
events.description: A largely bloodless coup by army officers ended the Estado Novo regime. Democracy followed, and Portugal's African colonies gained independence within two years.
